1	# Transition-state symmetry and molecular graph representations
2	
3	This task uses ordinary transition-state theory (TST) and the graph
4	representation conventions of the Auto-Mech project.  The following context is
5	provided as a method reference, not as a solution for this particular source
6	snapshot.
7	
8	For a reaction rate in canonical TST, a common schematic form is
9	
10	\[
11	k(T) = \frac{k_B T}{h}\frac{Q^\ddagger(T)}{Q_R(T)}
12	       \exp\left[-\frac{\Delta E^\ddagger}{k_B T}\right],
13	\]
14	
15	where the molecular partition functions contain translational, rotational, and
16	vibrational contributions. The rotational contribution for a nonlinear
17	molecule contains a symmetry divisor \(\sigma\):
18	
19	\[
20	q_{\mathrm{rot}} \propto \frac{1}{\sigma}
21	  \sqrt{I_A I_B I_C}\,T^{3/2},
22	\]
23	
24	with the corresponding expression for a linear molecule using its nonzero
25	moments of inertia. The symmetry number is a property of the physical
26	molecular object and its indistinguishable rotations; equivalent presentations
27	of one object must not change the physical factor. See Truhlar, Garrett, and
28	Klippenstein, *Current Status of Transition-State Theory*,
29	<https://doi.org/10.1021/cr00016a001>.
30	
31	Auto-Mech stores molecular connectivity as a graph: atom keys map to tuples
32	containing an element symbol, implicit-hydrogen count, and stereo information;
33	bonds are keyed by unordered atom-key pairs and carry bond-order information.
34	Transition-state graphs use the same representation while allowing an
35	intermediate bond order between the reactant and product limits to encode a
36	forming or breaking connection. The supplied graph APIs expose connectivity,
37	reaction orientation, and rotor-coordinate observations. These are
38	data-structure contracts, not assumptions about a particular fixture.
39	
40	For this workbench, a valid graph has finite atom and bond maps, unordered bond
41	keys, chemically consistent implicit-hydrogen counts, and finite transition
42	edge orders. A physical rotor observation is represented by a sorted signature
43	of canonical element-symbol sequences along the public coordinate objects. A
44	coordinate and its reverse describe the same unoriented physical axis, so the
45	lexicographically smaller sequence is used. Each physically distinct,
46	nonredundant rotatable axis must be represented once; removing an axis merely
47	to make two presentations have the same count is not a valid repair. Equivalent
48	graph presentations must produce the same signature exactly (these are
49	discrete symbols, so no numerical tolerance is involved), while the supplied
50	changed-connectivity negative control must not be collapsed to the same
51	observation. Distinguish that physical invariant from an implementation
52	artifact.
53	
54	## References
55	
56	1. D. G. Truhlar, B. C. Garrett, and S. J. Klippenstein, “Current Status of
57	   Transition-State Theory,” *Chemical Reviews* 100 (2000), 2703–2796,
58	   <https://doi.org/10.1021/cr00016a001>.
59	2. Auto-Mech project documentation and source docstrings at the supplied
60	   source commit, <https://github.com/Auto-Mech/autochem>.
61	
62	The supplied source is the historical version under investigation.  The task
63	does not require an external quantum-chemistry executable or internet access.

507	def ts_transferring_atoms(tsg) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]]:
508	    """Get get transferring atoms, along with their donors and acceptors
509	
510	    An atom is "transferring" if it is breaking and forming exactly one bond:
511	
512	        D---T...A
513	         (b) (f)
514	
515	    :param tsg: _description_
516	    :type tsg: _type_
517	    :returns: A dictionary mapping each transferring atom onto its donor (what it is
518	        transferring from) and its acceptor (what it is transferring to)
519	    :rtype: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]]
520	    """
521	    bkeys_dct = atoms_bond_keys(tsg)
522	    rxn_akeys = ts_reacting_atom_keys(tsg)
523	    frm_bkeys = ts_forming_bond_keys(tsg)
524	    brk_bkeys = ts_breaking_bond_keys(tsg)
525	
526	    tra_dct = {}
527	    for akey in rxn_akeys:
528	        afrm_bkeys = bkeys_dct[akey] & frm_bkeys
529	        abrk_bkeys = bkeys_dct[akey] & brk_bkeys
530	        if len(afrm_bkeys) == len(abrk_bkeys) == 1:
531	            (frm_bkey,) = afrm_bkeys
532	            (brk_bkey,) = abrk_bkeys
533	            (tra_key,) = brk_bkey & frm_bkey
534	            (don_key,) = brk_bkey - frm_bkey
535	            (acc_key,) = frm_bkey - brk_bkey
536	            tra_dct[tra_key] = (don_key, acc_key)
537	
538	    return tra_dct

143	def kekules_bond_orders(gra):
144	    """Bond orders for all possible low-spin kekule graphs
145	
146	    Low-spin kekule graphs have double and triple bonds assigned to
147	    minimize the number of unpaired electrons.
148	
149	    :param gra: molecular graph
150	    :type gra: automol graph data structure
151	    :returns: bond orders for all possible low-spin kekule graphs
152	    :rtype: tuple[dict]
153	    """
154	    assert not is_ts_graph(gra), f"This doesn't work for TS graphs:\n{gra}"
155	    gra = without_pi_bonds(gra)
156	    bord_dct0 = bond_orders(gra)
157	
158	    gra = implicit(gra)
159	
160	    # identify all of the independent pi systems and assign kekules to each
161	    pi_keys_lst = pi_system_atom_keys(gra)
162	    pi_bord_dcts_lst = [
163	        pi_system_kekules_bond_orders_brute_force(gra, pi_keys)
164	        for pi_keys in pi_keys_lst
165	    ]
166	
167	    bnd_ord_dcts = []
168	    # combine the kekules from each pi system together in all possible ways
169	    for bord_dcts in itertools.product(*pi_bord_dcts_lst):
170	        bord_dct = bord_dct0.copy()
171	        for dct in bord_dcts:
172	            bord_dct.update(dct)
173	        bnd_ord_dcts.append(bord_dct)
174	
175	    if bnd_ord_dcts:

    """Calculate the torsional normal modes at rotational bonds.

    :param geo: The geometry
    :param gra: A graph specifying the connectivity of the geometry
    :param bkeys: Specify the rotational bonds by index (ignores `with_x_rotors` flags);
        If `None`, they will be determined automatically
    :param mass_weight: Return mass-weighted normal modes?
    :param with_h_rotors: Include rotors neighbored by only hydrogens on one side?
    :param with_ch_rotors: Include rotors with C neighbored by only hydrogens?
    :return: The torsional normal modes, as a 3N x n_tors matrix
    """
    gra = graph(geo, stereo=False) if gra is None else gra
    bkeys = (
        graph_base.rotational_bond_keys(
            gra,
            with_h_rotors=with_h_rotors,
            with_ch_rotors=with_ch_rotors,
            with_rings_rotors=False,
        )
        if bkeys is None
        else bkeys
    )

    all_idxs = list(range(count(geo)))
    tors_coos = []
    for bkey in bkeys:
        axis_idxs = sorted(bkey)
        groups = graph_base.rotational_groups(gra, *axis_idxs)
        tors_ = torsional_motion_calculator_(geo, axis_idxs, groups)
        tors_coo = numpy.concatenate([tors_(idx) for idx in all_idxs])
        tors_coos.append(tors_coo)
    tors_coos = numpy.transpose(tors_coos)

    if mass_weight:
        tors_coos *= mass_weight_vector(geo)[:, numpy.newaxis]
    return tors_coos


def torsional_motion_calculator_(
    geo, axis_idxs: Sequence[int], groups: Sequence[Sequence[int]]
) -> Callable[[int], numpy.ndarray]:
    """Generate a torsional motion calculator.

    :param geo: The geometry
    :param axis_idxs: The indices of the rotational axis
    :param groups: The groups of the rotational axis
    """
    group1, group2 = groups
    xyz1, xyz2 = coordinates(geo, idxs=axis_idxs)
    axis1 = util.vector.unit_norm(numpy.subtract(xyz1, xyz2))
    axis2 = numpy.negative(axis1)

    def _torsional_motion(idx: int) -> numpy.ndarray:
        """Determine the torsional motion of an atom."""
        # If it is one of the axis atoms, it doesn't move
        if idx in axis_idxs:
            return numpy.zeros(3)
        # If it is in the first group, subtract and cross
        (xyz,) = coordinates(geo, idxs=(idx,))
        if idx in group1:
            dxyz = numpy.subtract(xyz, xyz1)
            return numpy.cross(dxyz, axis1)
        if idx in group2:
            dxyz = numpy.subtract(xyz, xyz2)
            return numpy.cross(dxyz, axis2)

        raise ValueError(f"{idx} not in {axis_idxs} {group1} {group2}")

    return _torsional_motion

def rotors_from_zmatrix(
    zma,
    gra=None,
    tor_names_lst: List[List[str]] = None,
    partition: bool = True,
    multi: bool = False,
) -> List[Rotor]:
    """Construct rotors by inferring torsions from the z-matrix and its graph

    :param zma: A z-matrix
    :type zma: automol zmat data structure
    :param gra: Optionally, specify the z-matrix connectivity with a graph
    :type gra: automol graph data structure
    :param tor_names_lst: A list of lists of torsion names identifying which torsions
        should be included and how they should be grouped
    :type tor_names_lst: List[List[str]]
    :param partition: Partition high-dimensional rotors? defaults to True
    :type partition: bool, optional
    :param multi: If no grouping was specified, group all torsions into a single rotor?
        Will be partitioned to reduce dimensionality if `partition=True` is set
    :type multi: bool, optional
    :returns: A list of rotors for this z-matrix
    :rtype: List[Rotor]
    """
    gra = zmat.graph(zma, stereo=True, dummy=True) if gra is None else gra
    lin_keys = graph.linear_atom_keys(gra, dummy=True)
    znkeys_dct = zmat.neighbor_keys(zma)

    rot_bkeys = graph.rotational_bond_keys(gra, lin_keys=lin_keys)

    # Read in the torsion coordinate names and sort them in z-matrix order
    tor_names = [zmat.torsion_coordinate_name(zma, *bk) for bk in rot_bkeys]
    tor_names = [n for n in zmat.dihedral_angle_names(zma) if n in tor_names]

    tor_lst = []
    for name in tor_names:
        tor_keys = list(reversed(zmat.coordinate(zma, name)))
        tor_axis = tor_keys[1:3]
        tor = tors.from_data(
            name_=name,
            coo=tor_keys,
            grps=graph.rotational_groups(gra, *tor_axis),
            symm=graph.rotational_symmetry_number(gra, *tor_axis, lin_keys=lin_keys),
            ngrps=list(map(znkeys_dct.get, tor_axis)),
        )
        tor_lst.append(tor)

    return rotors_from_data(
        zma=zma,
        tor_lst=tor_lst,
        tor_names_lst=tor_names_lst,
        partition=partition,
        multi=multi,
    )

def rotors_zmatrix(rotors: List[Rotor]):
    """Get the z-matrix associated with a list of rotors

    Requires that all z-matrices match exactly

    :param rotors: A list of rotor objects
    :type rotors: List[Rotor]
    :returns: The z-matrix
    :rtype: automol zmat data structure
    """
    if not rotors:
        return None

    zmas = list(map(zmatrix, rotors))
    zma, *zmas = zmas
    assert all(zma == z for z in zmas)
    return zma

def external_symmetry_factor(geo, chiral_center=True):
    """Obtain the external symmetry factor for a geometry using MolSym

    If requested, divides by the enantiomeric factor

    :param geo: molecular geometry
    :type geo: automol geometry data structure
    :rtype: float
    """

    if is_atom(geo):

    else:

        ext_sym_fac = _0molsym.point_group_symmetry_number(pg_obj)
        if _0molsym.point_group_is_chiral(pg_obj) and chiral_center:

    return ext_sym_fac

def apply_zmatrix_conversion(geo, zc_: ZmatConv, gra=None, dist: float = 1.0):
    """Apply a z-matrix conversion to this geometry, inserting dummy atoms and
    reordering as described in a z-matrix conversion data structure

    :param geo: A molecular geometry
    :type geo: automol geom data structure
    :param zc_: A z-matrix conversion
    :type zc_: ZmatConv
    :param gra: A molecular graph, defaults to None
    :type gra: automol graph data structure, optional
    :param dist: The distance of the dummy atom to its parent atom, in Angstroms,
        defaults to 1.0
    :type dist: float, optional
    :returns: The transformed molecular geometry
    :rtype: automol geom data structure
    """
    lin_keys = zmat_conv.linear_atom_keys(zc_, "geom")
    dir_key_dct = dict(zmat_conv.dummy_source_keys(zc_, "geom"))
    gra = graph_without_stereo(geo) if gra is None else gra

    # Partition parent atoms into adjacent segments
    lin_seg_dct = graph_base.linear_segment_cap_keys(gra, lin_keys=lin_keys)
    # lin_seg_keys_lst = graph_base.linear_segments_atom_keys(gra, lin_keys=lin_keys)

    # Build an initial z-matrix conversion data structure to describe the insertion
    nreal = count(geo)
    lin_gkeys = list(itertools.chain(*lin_seg_dct.keys()))
    zc0 = zmat_conv.from_geom_data(nreal, lin_gkeys)

    # Identify a perpendicular direction for each segment and insert the dummy atoms
    # (Parent atom indices don't change, since the dummy atoms are added to the end)
    xyzs = coordinates(geo, angstrom=True)
    for seg_keys, cap_keys in lin_seg_dct.items():
        key1, key2 = cap_keys
        if key1 == key2:
            key1, *_ = seg_keys
            key2 = dir_key_dct[key1]
        xyz1, xyz2 = coordinates(geo, idxs=(key1, key2))
        dir_vec = vector.unit_norm(numpy.subtract(xyz2, xyz1))
        dum_vec = vector.arbitrary_unit_perpendicular(dir_vec)
        for idx in seg_keys:
            xyz = numpy.add(xyzs[idx], numpy.multiply(dist, dum_vec))
            geo = insert(geo, "X", xyz, angstrom=True)

    # Reorder the geometry to match the desired conversion
    geo = reorder(geo, zmat_conv.isomorphism(zc0, zc_))
    return geo

def signature(g, coords):
    symbols = graph.atom_symbols(g)
    sigs = []
    for item in coords:
        seq = tuple(symbols[k] for k in item)
        sigs.append(min(seq, seq[::-1]))

def rand_graph(rng, n_atoms, n_react):
    keys = list(range(1, n_atoms + 1))
    symbs = [rng.choice(list(VAL)) for _ in range(n_atoms)]
    atoms = {k: (s, 0, None) for k, s in zip(keys, symbs)}
    deg = {k: 0 for k in keys}
    bonds = {}

    def can_add(a, b):
        bk = frozenset({a, b})
        return bk not in bonds and deg[a] < VAL[atoms[a][0]] and deg[b] < VAL[atoms[b][0]]

    order = keys[:]
    rng.shuffle(order)
    for i in range(1, n_atoms):
        k = order[i]
        cands = [j for j in order[:i] if can_add(k, j)]
        if not cands:
            return None
        j = rng.choice(cands)
        bk = frozenset({k, j})
        bonds[bk] = (1, None)
        deg[k] += 1
        deg[j] += 1
    for _ in range(n_atoms):

        if not pairs:

        bk = frozenset({a, b})
        bonds[bk] = (1, None)
        deg[a] += 1
        deg[b] += 1
    bks = sorted(bonds, key=lambda b: sorted(b))
    n = min(n_react, len(bks))

    mp = dict(zip(keys, new))

        {frozenset(mp[k] for k in bk): v for bk, v in g[1].items()},
    )


def signature(g, coords):
    syms = graph.atom_symbols(g)
    out = []
    for c in coords:
        seq = tuple(syms[k] for k in c)
        out.append(min(seq, seq[::-1]))
    return sorted(out)
